steps.title: Rubber-duck it
steps.statement: Explaining your code line by line, out loud, to anyone (even a rubber duck) makes you notice the step you skipped.

explain.text: Three moves: trace your steps and ask whether you skipped one; explain each line out loud and why you chose that function; be descriptive, which is also how you ask for help online. Saying what a line should do forces you to compare it with what it does.

terms.meaning: finding a bug by explaining the code aloud, step by step

steps.intuition: Speaking slows you down to the speed of the bug.
steps.misconception: You need an expert to find a bug. Explaining it precisely, to anyone, finds most of them.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: Only an expert can spot it.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Saying each line aloud exposes it.

check.q: Why does a precise description also help when asking online?
check.a: Others can only help with what you state: the code, the message and what you expected.

steps.answers: What do you do when you cannot see the bug?
steps.opens: Which graph shows your data best?
